recommendation:
**R0 — The tension resolves by changing the access verb: filter, don't read.** `index.md` and `map.md` are *read*, so context cost is O(corpus) — image-maze's index alone is 4,543 tokens (vault-reality B). Make the primary navigation artifact one that agents `rg` instead of `cat`. Then disk size scales with knowledge (goals 1–2) while context cost stays flat (goal 3). That is the whole design.

**R1 — Artifact: `<vault>/_meta/routes.tsv`, generated, gitignored, never committed.** One row per page: `path\tkind\tupdated\tinbound\tbytes\tsummary(<=120c)\tkeywords`. New mode `wiki_lint.py --write-routes`. Every field already exists: page/graph enumeration at `body/wiki_lint.py:222-241`, dates via `git_date` (`:113-121`), kind from directory (`body/SKILL.md:96-104` — "the directory supplies the page kind"), summary by deterministic first-sentence extraction, keywords from the page's `##` lines. Zero hand-maintained state, so it generalises CONCEPT.md's "computed triggers, never recorded triggers" to computed *artifacts*.
Why untracked is mandatory, not stylistic: `runner/run-promotion.sh:169-176` fails on any new non-Markdown file in the vault, and `:44-60` requires `--untracked-files=all` clean. Gitignored + rebuild-when-older-than-newest-`.md` makes it a **cache**. A cache cannot go stale the way `map.md` did, and it touches no gate. It is also invisible to lint (`rglob("*.md")`, `:222`). Size: 155 rows ≈ 14 KB on disk; a filtered query returns 5–20 rows ≈ 150–500 tokens.

**R2 — The agent's first move**, one line in `bc-init-agent/body/scaffold.py:163` replacing "Read `index.md` → this file → `map.md`":
`rg -i '<2-4 task words>' .agent/_meta/routes.tsv | head -20` → open 2–3 paths.
On miss: `qmd search` (BM25, no models). **Never `qmd query`** — measured 67.1 s (vault-reality B) while `concepts/qmd/body/SKILL.md:29-33` advertises `--no-rerank ≈ 20s`; that deployed figure is 3.4× optimistic and should be corrected.
Last resort: `head -14 routes.tsv`, which the generator orders by inbound degree — Brain's prefilled compact index, computed rather than written, ≈350 tokens. `index.md` stops being an agent entry point and stays the curated editorial catalog, so CONCEPT.md's curated-not-generated decision is untouched: I generate a *different* file.

**R3 — `map.md`: demote, don't delete.** It is precisely the stale-hand-maintained-marker failure, already realised. image-maze's map lists architecture-runway rounds 4–7 while rounds 8 and 9 exist on disk. Music's map is still the scaffold default with no section for `findings/`, `decisions/`, `components/`, `plans/`, `open-questions/` — 34 of its 69 pages. And because map.md writes targets as backticked code spans, `without_code` (`wiki_lint.py:23-40`) masks them before `links()` (`:71-79`), so **map.md contributes zero graph edges and lint never validates it**. `references/wordpress-local-env.md` appears in image-maze's map twice, is absent from `index.md`, and is on the orphan list.

**R4 — Orphans: keep as a smell, drop as a goal.** Once routes.tsv covers every page by construction, every page is 1-hop reachable, so zero-inbound stops meaning unreachable. Replace the goal metric with first-move hit rate. **No automatic prose linker**: Gate 1's byte-prefix check (`run-promotion.sh:186-210`) mechanically rejects inserting a link into existing prose, and Music (197 wikilinks, still 12 orphans) shows density does not fix orphanhood anyway. Convention: **Markdown links everywhere** — 8/9 vaults already are, they render on the public Homeflix repo, and rewriting Music's 197 is forbidden by Gate 1, so converge by attrition. Reject `[cite:N]`: hand-numbered evidence edges are the recorded-state failure mode. Take Brain's evidence edge cheaply instead — a promoted dated section quotes the exact `## [YYYY-MM-DD]` log heading it came from (additive; one line in `SKILL.md` §3).

**R5 — Page contract, reconciled.** CONCEPT.md rejected frontmatter because a hand-maintained `updated` duplicates Git. A summary line duplicates nothing and is underivable. Contract: line 1 `# Title`, line 3 one sentence ≤200 chars. No date field, no status field — freshness stays `git_date`. Lint checks shape, not truth, and warns only, because Gate 1 forbids retrofitting line 3 into existing pages; legacy rows fall back to first-sentence extraction. Size: warn above 12 KB, **never auto-split** (a split is a rewrite). Instead emit section rows for oversized pages, so `project/architecture-module-map.md` (70,757 B ≈ 17.7 k tokens) becomes reachable at ~500 tokens per section without editing a byte.

**R6 — Cadence, split by operation.** Route cache: on demand, mtime-invalidated, ~1 s, no LLM, no timer. Lint: nightly, already 8 vaults — add dng as the 9th. Promotion: **stay nightly batch, become list-driven**. Today's no-ops are a coverage bug: the four vaults holding promotion timers have 1 unpromoted heading between them, while the five without hold 68. One unit looping `~/.config/agent-concepts/wiki-lint-vaults.txt` replaces four per-vault units and takes coverage 4/9 → 9/9; no-ops already cost nothing (`run-promotion.sh:114-120` exits before invoking Pi). Not end-of-session: `:44-60` requires a clean worktree, which mid-session rarely is.

**R7 — Safety.** No gate relaxes, none changes. The cache is untracked and non-Markdown, so it sits outside all three by construction. List-driven promotion raises frequency, not per-run authority: classification coverage (`wiki_lint.py:365-419`) and byte-prefix additivity (`run-promotion.sh:186-210`) apply per vault unchanged. New risk it introduces: sql and Scripts emit `PROMOTION_RANGE=invalid` and the wrapper `fail`s (`:104-107`), so the loop must skip-and-report per vault and never abort the batch — mirroring `run-lint.sh`'s continue-on-failure.

**R8 — Sequence, and the one number.** (1) `--write-routes` + the scaffold first-move line. Number: **median tokens loaded between vault entry and opening the correct page over a fixed 20-question benchmark; baseline 4,543 (image-maze index) / 1,746 (homeflix-prod); target ≤800.** (2) List-driven promotion. Number: total unpromoted headings across 9 vaults, 69 → <10 within 14 nights. (3) Section rows for >12 KB pages. (4) Summary line in scaffold templates, new pages only. All four are one-script or one-unit changes that apply to all nine vaults without per-vault hand-holding.

A generated file inside the vault cannot be committed or even left untracked: the wrapper fails on new non-Markdown files and refuses to run on a dirty tree including untracked files. Hence the route table must be gitignored.
An automatic prose linker is already mechanically forbidden: the wrapper requires committed bytes to remain an exact prefix of the new file for any tracked vault file with deleted lines.

assumptions.assumption: qmd search (BM25) really costs ~0.5s on these vaults; only qmd query was measured at 67.1s.
ripgrep over a keyword-bearing TSV reaches the right page for most real questions. No hit-rate benchmark exists yet; this is the design's load-bearing empirical bet.
File mtime is a reliable cache-invalidation signal under Syncthing (all nine vaults live under /home/ben/Sync).
A gitignore entry for _meta/routes.tsv is acceptable in the public Homeflix repo.
Deterministic first-sentence extraction yields usable summaries for legacy pages; the sampled openings are mixed (vault-reality §D shows H1+blank, frontmatter, and blockquote openings).
_meta/routes.tsv is invisible to lint because page enumeration is rglob('*.md') — read from wiki_lint.py:222, not executed.

risks: rg hit rate is the single point of failure. If keywords miss, the agent falls back to a 350-token hub head and then to index.md, which is no worse than today but delivers none of the win.

Making promotion list-driven points an unattended writer at five vaults it has never touched, including Music's 37-heading backlog. A first run there is large and judgment-heavy; consider a first-run cap or a manual first pass per vault.
sql and Scripts will fail nightly on PROMOTION_RANGE=invalid (13 bare headings). Without skip-and-report the batch aborts and the other seven vaults silently stop being maintained.

Deterministic summaries can be actively misleading (image-maze's architecture-module-map.md opens 'Status: Current'), and a wrong one-liner is worse than none because it is trusted at the routing step.
Untracked cache files under Syncthing may produce conflict copies (.sync-conflict-*.tsv) that are neither gitignored by name nor cleaned up.
Section rows multiply table size on oversized pages; image-maze's 70KB module map alone could add dozens of rows, eroding the flat-cost property for rg queries that match its keywords broadly.

confidence.reason: The diagnosis is verified directly against source (map.md's code-span targets vs without_code/links; the gate mechanics in run-promotion.sh; timer coverage vs backlog distribution). The prescription's core bet — that rg over a generated keyword TSV reaches the right page cheaply — is unmeasured, and no first-move benchmark exists on this machine. The cadence and safety recommendations are high-confidence; the read-path artifact is a medium-confidence design that ships with its own falsification test.

challengeClaims: Any full-corpus catalog an agent *reads* costs >=3,500 tokens at image-maze's 155 pages (~25 tokens/row). If your design has the agent read a generated navigation page, state its token size at 155 pages and show the margin over index.md's measured 4,543 that justifies building it.

Any design that inserts links into existing prose is rejected by run-promotion.sh:186-210, which requires committed bytes to remain an exact byte prefix. Name the mechanism by which your automatic linker lands, or concede it requires changing Gate 1 and state the rewrite failure mode you are reopening.

The four vaults with promotion timers hold 1 unpromoted heading between them; the five without hold 68. If you propose end-of-session or continuous triggers, explain why that beats pointing the existing nightly unit at all nine vaults, given run-promotion.sh:44-60 refuses to run on a dirty worktree.
ownerDecisions: Whether _meta/routes.tsv is gitignored inside each vault (discoverable by a cold agent) or written to ~/.cache/ (invisible but never near a commit). Public Homeflix makes this a repo-policy call, not a technical one.
Whether map.md is demoted to human-editorial or removed from the scaffold entirely. Removal is cleaner but deletes content in nine live vaults, which no automated pass may do.

Whether to spend one human edit normalising the 13 bare '## YYYY-MM-DD' headings in sql and Scripts. CONCEPT.md deliberately requires a human act on the append-only log; the design does not change that, it just makes the failure louder nightly.
Whether dng (unregistered qmd drift, absent from wiki-lint-vaults.txt) gets registered or documented as an intentional exclusion.
Whether Music's first list-driven promotion run (37 headings) goes unattended or is run manually once first.
changeMyMind: A 20-question benchmark showing rg-over-routes.tsv misses the correct page more than ~30% of the time. Then filter-don't-read fails and the right answer is a small read-a-generated-index design, or a cheap local embedding first move.

A measurement showing qmd search (BM25) is genuinely ~0.5s and hits well on these corpora. Then routes.tsv shrinks to a fallback for the 3 unregistered vaults, and the primary fix is a one-line change to the scaffold's first move plus registering dng.

Evidence that file mtime is unreliable under Syncthing here. Then the cache cannot self-invalidate, it must be committed, and that reopens the non-Markdown-file gate — which would push me toward generating routes as a Markdown page under _meta/ that maintenance_report() (wiki_lint.py:206) already excludes from orphan and index checks.

A measured session trace showing agents do not currently load index.md first (i.e. the 4,543-token baseline is hypothetical). Then the read-path win is smaller than claimed and sequencing should start with list-driven promotion instead.
